'''Toby Hemenway''' (April 23, 1952 – December 20, 2016)<ref name="Press Democrat">{{cite news |last1=Mason |first1=Clark |title=Toby Hemenway, leading permaculture promoter, dies at 64 |url=https://www.pressdemocrat.com/news/6462483-181/toby-hemenway-leading-permaculture-promoter |accessdate=24 August 2019 |work=Santa Rosa Press Democrat |date=22 December 2016 |language=en}}</ref> was an American author and educator who wrote extensively on [[permaculture]] and [[ecological]] issues. He was the author of ''Gaia's Garden: A Guide to Home-Scale Permaculture'' and ''The Permaculture City: Regenerative Design for Urban, Suburban, and Town Resilience''. He served as an adjunct professor at [[Portland State University]], Scholar-in-Residence at [[Pacific University]], and field director at the Permaculture Institute (USA).<ref name=PDMTH />

==Career==
After obtaining a degree in biology from [[Tufts University]], Hemenway worked for many years as a researcher in genetics and immunology, first in academic laboratories including [[Harvard]] and the [[University of Washington]] in Seattle.<ref name=RTH /> He also worked at [[Immunex]], a major medical biotech company.<ref name="Press Democrat" />

At about the time he was growing dissatisfied with the direction biotechnology was taking, he discovered permaculture. A career change followed, and Hemenway and his wife, Kiel, spent ten years creating a rural permaculture site in [[southern Oregon]]. He was the editor of ''Permaculture Activist'', a journal of ecological design and sustainable culture, from 1999 to 2004.<ref name=RTH>{{cite web |url= https://www.resilience.org/stories/2016-12-21/appreciating-toby-hemenway-1952-2016/ |title= Appreciating Toby Hemenway 1952-2016 |last= Heinberg |first= Richard |date= 21 December 2016 |website= Resilience |publisher= |access-date= November 20, 2025 |quote=}}</ref> He moved to [[Portland, Oregon]] in 2004, and after six years of developing urban sustainability resources there, Hemenway and his wife divided their time between [[Sebastopol, California]] and [[western Montana]].

Hemenway died of pancreatic cancer on December 20, 2016.<ref name=PDMTH>{{cite web |url= https://www.permaculturedesignmagazine.com/post/2016/12/21/author-of-gaias-garden-dies |title= Author of Gaia's Garden Dies |last= Bane |first= Peter |date= 21 December 2016 |website= Permaculture Design Magazine |publisher= |access-date= November 20, 2025 |quote=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://tobyhemenway.com/1431-tobys-battle-with-cancer-update/|title=Update on Toby Hemenway's Battle With Cancer|date=December 19, 2016|website=Toby Hemenway}}</ref>

The Permaculture Skills Center in California opened a Toby Hemenway Memorial Library using the author’s personal collection.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://permacultureskillscenter.org/toby-hemenway-memorial-library/ |title= Toby Hemenway, April 23, 1952 – December 20, 2016 |last= |first= |date= |website= Permaculture Skills Center |publisher= |access-date= November 20, 2025 |quote=}}</ref>
